physical_mismatches.reason: Cooling mismatch: the paper uses a fin-channel air-forced heatsink (30 mm fin height, 1 mm fin width, 10 cm fan radius, 5000 rpm, lateral airflow), a 5 mm spreader edge, a 20 mm heatsink edge and 318.5 K ambient. A simplified Studio package with a generic convective boundary will not reproduce this HotSpot fan and heatsink model.

Interposer stack mismatch: the paper models a six-layer stack (FR-4 organic substrate, C4 bumps, silicon interposer with TSVs, microbumps, chiplet layer, TIM) with detailed bump and TSV parameters that are not published in the packet. A simplified Studio layer stack cannot reproduce the vertical heat paths.
Solver mismatch: HotSpot's compact RC network (grid of nodes) differs from a different steady-state solver, so absolute temperatures will not match 373.58 K exactly.

Block geometry is available only as grid-map figures (Figure 9b) with theoretical sizes that include spacing. Absolute block positions are not published numerically, so the same-scenario layout cannot be reconstructed without digitising.
The CMO optimizer and its weight alpha are not reproduced by a thermal solver. They only generated the layout, so this is not a thermal mismatch if the published layout is fixed.
No controller, transient workload or reliability analysis is part of the selected scenario, so these are not mismatches. The scenario is a steady, static 2.5-D placement, not 3D stacking.

studio_assumptions: The packet does not specify the bundled Studio package, materials or boundary conditions, so none are assumed here.
Power is treated as uniform over each chiplet, as the paper states (PDF page 4, Section 3.2.1).
Chiplet surface temperature is treated as equal to the chiplet overall temperature, as the paper states (PDF page 4).
